account:
Today I have been keeping my appointments: morning office business, the ten o'clock mill inspection, lunch at home, and now council letters at town hall. At the mill stall I personally saw 128 hay bales, but I did not obtain a keeper's confirmation of storage conditions or deliveries. Several townsfolk repeated unusually vague news about a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery and said the baker had carried a sack of bread. I have no reliable description of any actual change, and cannot infer a disruption from those reports alone. Neighbour was at the bakery, but my questions have not yet produced a clear explanation. We are due for tea at the east-dock cottage at fifteen.

The secretary has obtained the writable office book after I provided one emerald for stationery, separate from the agreed two-emerald inspection fee. She has arranged to transcribe Builder's findings at sixteen, before my sixteen-thirty review. Builder has just arrived early and reported inn work: a normally operating door and one authorized lantern fitted clear of the passage for four emeralds, which he says was paid in full. He explicitly has not verified sleeping arrangements or certified guest readiness. This appears to concern lighting and preparing the inn, but I do not know who commissioned it or whether it relates to the bakery rumours. The secretary is coordinating the written record, and I am awaiting her answer about council correspondence. I should keep confirmed observations separate from rumours and Builder's reported work separate from any town expenditure I have authorized.
